newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may exempt all foreign capital from CPMF.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may exempt all foreign capital from CPMF.

text.p: The Brazilian government may still exempt all foreign stock investments from a new financial transaction tax, a Finance Ministry official said.
Executive secretary Pedro Parente said the government was still considering whether to exempt from the so-called CPMF tax foreign capital inflows and outflows from Brazilian bourses.
Earlier, Parente announced that foreigners would have to pay the 0.2 percent levy on the start and the end of stock market investments but not on transactions in between.
A Finance Ministry spokesman said after Parente's briefing that the tax on inflows and outflows "might still be revoked if that was found to be necessary".
The new tax, designed to raise 400 million reais a month for the health services, comes into effect on January 23, not on January 25 as previously expected.
Officials had expressed concern it could lead to capital flight unless foreign investment in stocks was made exempt.
A decree setting the rules for the CPMF is expected to be published soon, possibly on Monday.
